Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Ogier Ghislain de Busbecq (author, Wikidata Q647633), died 1592; Pierre Bayle (other, Wikidata Q214816), died 1706. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Busbecq, Ogier Ghislain de, 1522-1592; Bayle, Pierre, 1647-1706 [Contributor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Travels into Turkey: containing the most accurate account of the Turks, and neighbouring nations, ... Translated from the original latin of the learned A. G. Busbequius. ...  1744, 1744, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_travels-into-turkey-con_busbecq-ogier-ghislain-_1744. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 88%, 57%, 89% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Ogier Ghislain de Busbecq, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
